issue.title: Linker error when building with libc++
issue.body:
I'm currently trying to compile MAVSDK with llvms libc++ instead of libstdc++, due to compatibility reasons with another framework (Unreal Engine) . 

Building of most targets actually succeeds, but I can't perform an install due to linker errors in 2 components.

My CMake commands:
```sh
cmake ./MAVSDK -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=17 \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} -pthread -stdlib=libc++ -std=c++17 -lc++abi" \
    -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS} -pthread -stdlib=libc++ -std=c++17 -lc++abi" \
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=./ \
    -Bbuild/default 

cmake --build build/default --target install -j 6
```

OS: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
APT Version of clang & libc++abi

comments.body:
We have this (unrelated but similar) `BUILD_STATIC_MAVSDK_SERVER` flag where we define `-static-libstdc++`. It appears in 3 CMakeLists.txt, including `src/mavsdk_server/test/CMakeLists.txt`.

Maybe you could try hardcoding your flags around that flag (not in the `if BUILD_STATIC_MAVSDK_SERVER` obviously, because by default this is not enabled, but put it close to it) and see if that helps?

Thanks for the suggestion, but I didn't really want to modify the internal CMake files of MAVSDK for CI/CD reasons. 
To still make it work, I ended up only building the `mavsdk` target and copying the library and headers manually. It now successfully links against my Unreal Engine project.

If anyone else has a similar use-case, this is the script I'm using to replace the `install` target:
https://gist.github.com/LarsLeferenz/11b05b8ff8e1255e9b6c29d21d044bfe

I can't guarantee that all plugins will link, as I only need `telemetry` for now.

> Thanks for the suggestion, but I didn't really want to modify the internal CMake files of MAVSDK for CI/CD reasons.

I was mostly asking in an informative way: would be nice to know what it takes to make it work.

Ran into the same issue when integrating MAVSDK with unreal on ubuntu 22.

For me, on Unreal 5.5, this worked for me:

1. Add these flags on top of CMakeLists.txt (obviously change the path of these to be the path of your unreal engine c++ stuff, right now the paths are set to mine)

```
set(CMAKE_C_COMPILER "/home/john/repos/Linux_Unreal_Engine_5.5.0/Engine/Extras/ThirdPartyNotUE/SDKs/HostLinux/Linux_x64/v23_clang-18.1.0-rockylinux8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/clang")
set(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER "/home/john/repos/Linux_Unreal_Engine_5.5.0/Engine/Extras/ThirdPartyNotUE/SDKs/HostLinux/Linux_x64/v23_clang-18.1.0-rockylinux8/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/clang++")

# Disable system C++ standard library
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} -nostdinc++")

# Use Unreal's libc++
set(UNREAL_LIBCXX_INCLUDE "/home/john/repos/Linux_Unreal_Engine_5.5.0/Engine/Source/ThirdParty/Unix/LibCxx/include/c++/v1")
set(UNREAL_LIBCXX_LIB "/home/john/repos/Linux_Unreal_Engine_5.5.0/Engine/Source/ThirdParty/Unix/LibCxx/lib/Unix/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")

# Add libc++ includes manually
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} -I${UNREAL_LIBCXX_INCLUDE}")
```

Note: there's probably some stuff not necessary that I added to cmake, was trying a bunch of things

2. Run command
`cmake -Bbuild/default -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON BUILD_TESTING=OFF -S.
`

If build testing is on, the build will fail.

3. `cmake --build build/default/ -j14`

4. Now put the generated shared object and headers in your unreal project and link them like you normally would.

This dynamic linking works for me.

---


As a note, I tried using static linking by setting -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF but first ran into linker errors with libstdc++ for many of the built third party libraries in MAVSDK (I fixed this by manually setting the same CMAKE options above for those other cmake files).

But even when fixing that, I always ran into the following error:
`0>ld.lld: Error  : undefined symbol: pthread_cond_clockwait
0>>>> referenced by mavsdk_impl.cpp`

Which appears to be caused by some incompatibility with MAVSDK and the glibc version unreal uses.

So, static linking doesn't seem to work for now. Will see what I can do (if it's worth the effort for me)
